title: Review: Pressure and hydrostatics; Upthrust / Archimedes' principle; SI units and prefixes; Graphs and data analysis; Estimation and orders of magnitude; Experimental methods and practical skills
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: MS06-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; MS06-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; MS06-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; MS01-1#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: FL02-1#N.3, FL03-1#N.7, MS01-1#N.5, MS04-1#N.10, MS06-1#N.13, FL02-1#N.2, FL03-1#N.4b, MS01-1#N.7, MS04-1#N.6, MS06-1#N.12, FL02-1#N.10, MS01-1#N.12. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Control variables
items.clue: Everything else that could affect the result, kept fixed.

items.label: Independent variable
items.clue: The one quantity you deliberately change in an experiment.

items.label: Conclusion
items.clue: Statement of what the data show, only within the range tested.

items.label: Derived unit
items.clue: One obtained from a defining equation, such as m s⁻¹ for velocity.

questions.stem: A sealed container holds a gas at a pressure of 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa. Which statement about this pressure is correct?

options.text: The gas presses mainly on the base of the container, because gas pressure acts downwards.
Pressure is a vector, so the pressures acting on opposite walls of the container cancel out.
The gas exerts a force of 1.0 × 10⁵ N on each wall, whatever the area of that wall.
The gas pushes perpendicular to every wall, exerting 1.0 × 10⁵ N on each square metre of wall.

questions.stem: A foam ball of volume V would float, but it is held at rest completely under water by a light string tied to the bottom of a tank. The density of the foam is a quarter of the density ρ of water. Which expression gives the tension in the string?
A spring's stiffness is its spring constant: the force needed per unit change in its length. What is the unit of the spring constant in base units?
questions.explanation: Spring constant = force ÷ change in length: kg m s⁻² ÷ m = kg s⁻². This is the same unit as N m⁻¹.

questions.stem: A classroom is about 8 m long, 6 m wide and 3 m high. What is the order of magnitude of the mass of air in it?
questions.explanation: Volume ≈ 8 × 6 × 3 = 144 m³. Mass ≈ 144 × 1.2 ≈ 170 kg, order 10² kg.

questions.stem: A student has a ruler with 1 mm divisions and wants the thickness of one sheet of paper, about 0.1 mm. Which choice and reason are both correct?

options.text: Measure one sheet ten times and average, because averaging reduces the uncertainty.
Measure a stack of 200 sheets and divide by 200, because the reading uncertainty is shared out.
Measure a stack of 10 sheets ten times and average, because more readings always help.
Measure a stack of 200 sheets and divide by 200, because any calibration error in the ruler then cancels.

questions.stem: A force of 50 N acts on a flat plate of area 25 cm². The force is at 60° to the plate's surface. What pressure does the force exert on the plate?
questions.explanation: The angle is from the surface, so the perpendicular component is 50 sin 60° = 43.3 N. A = 25 × 10⁻⁴ m², so pressure = 43.3 ÷ 2.5 × 10⁻³ = 1.7 × 10⁴ Pa.

questions.stem: Two solid balls of equal volume, one made of lead and one of aluminum, hang from strings so that each is completely under water at the same depth. Lead is denser than aluminum. How does the buoyant force on the lead ball compare with the buoyant force on the aluminum ball?

options.text: Greater on the lead ball, since it has the greater mass
Greater on the aluminum ball, since it is the less dense
Zero on both, since both would sink if released
Equal, since the balls displace equal volumes of water

questions.stem: The cross-sectional area of a wire is 0.50 mm². What is this area in m²?
What is the best estimate of the volume of water in a full bath?
questions.explanation: About 1.5 m × 0.6 m × 0.4 m ≈ 0.4 m³ (about 400 litres).

questions.stem: A student investigates how the time t for a ball to fall from rest depends on the drop height h. (h = ½gt², with g constant.) Which plan is best?

options.text: Drop the ball once from each of three heights, timing by hand; plot t against h.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t.
Drop the ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically; plot h against t².
Drop a ball three times from each of six heights, timing electronically, with a heavier ball for the greater heights.

questions.explanation: Enough values, repeats, no reaction time, and h = (g/2)t² gives a straight line through the origin with gradient g/2.

questions.stem: A fluid at pressure P pushes on a circular piston of radius r and exerts a force of magnitude F on it, perpendicular to the piston. The same fluid pressure acts on a second circular piston of radius 2r. The magnitude of the force on the second piston is how many times F?
Pressure is force ÷ area, and its unit is the pascal (Pa). What is the pascal in base units?
questions.explanation: Pa = N m⁻² = kg m s⁻² × m⁻² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻².
